original_question: Must every rational map that has a Herman ring also have buried Julia components, or are additional global dynamical or topological assumptions needed before the existence of a Herman ring forces buried Julia components to appear?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in the introduction, read together with Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3, concerning whether the presence of a Herman ring forces a nonempty residual Julia set / buried Julia component for a rational map under the paper's stated hypotheses.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main objects in play: rational maps, Herman rings, and buried Julia phenomena, and it correctly frames the issue as an implication question rather than as a request for examples or classification. It is also close in spirit to the paper's introductory open problem.
missing_details: The paper's question is about rational self-maps of the Riemann sphere, not arbitrary meromorphic maps.
The degree condition should be stated explicitly: a rational map of degree at least 2.
The paper's formulation is narrower than your draft because it includes a global hypothesis on the Julia set; the key missing restriction is that the Julia set is disconnected.
'Herman ring' should be defined as a periodic doubly connected Fatou component on which an iterate is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of an annulus.
'Buried Julia component' should be defined explicitly as a connected component of the Julia set that does not meet the boundary of any Fatou component.
Proposition 1.2 supplies the paper's precise reformulation, so the question should mention the residual Julia set formulation if that is the paper's official equivalent version.
The quantifier should be fully explicit: the question asks whether every rational map satisfying all of those hypotheses must satisfy the buried-component conclusion.
Your draft is broader than the paper because it asks whether extra assumptions might be needed; in the paper those assumptions are already built into the official formulation.
refined_question: Let f be a rational map of degree at least 2 on the Riemann sphere whose Julia set J(f) is disconnected. If f has a Herman ring, must J(f) contain a buried Julia component?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under the same hypotheses, must the residual Julia set J_r(f) be nonempty?
justification: The introduction isolates this as an explicit conjectural question, and the nearby Proposition 1.2 is used to sharpen the wording by giving the paper's equivalent reformulation in terms of the residual Julia set. Theorem 1.3 is presented as supporting evidence/partial progress for that same introductory problem, so the faithful stand-alone version should keep the paper's ambient setting (rational maps on the Riemann sphere), the disconnectedness assumption on J(f), and the exact buried/residual-Julia-set language rather than the broader wording of your draft.
